newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes stronger vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes stronger vs dollar.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed stronger against the dollar on Monday as banks began to sell the U.S. currency despite the Central Bank holding positive towards it, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 59.10 to the dollar after opening at 59.20. On Friday, it closed at 59.23.
"Selling pressure has been building up despite the Central Bank's positive stand towards the dollar," said a local bank dealer.
On Monday, the Central Bank pushed the dollar-rupee exchange rate down only marginally, by quarter local cent, despite the dollar's substantial falls overseas.
It fixed buying and selling rates at 58.2170 and 59.3931.
"True, the Central Bank is pushing the dollar up. But when they are carrying plus positions, banks are a bit uncomfortable," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
As the dollar came down, local banks carrying dollar plus positions began to sell, bringing the greenback down against the rupee, he said.
Overnight call money, which opened at 9.5 percent, closed at 11 percent.
